task_2.title: Avoid collection crashes from unreadable unselected directories
task_2.description: The update fixes a runtime collection failure in pytest when an unreadable directory exists in the project tree but is not part of the command-line selection. Instead of aborting collection with a PermissionError while checking whether that directory is a Python package, pytest should ignore that directory and continue collecting the explicitly requested tests.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running pytest against selected test paths does not crash when unrelated directories in the project tree are unreadable.

expectation.grounded: During directory collection, pytest should treat a PermissionError raised while checking whether a directory contains a package initializer as a non-collectable directory and continue processing the command-line-selected test targets. If the unreadable directory is not selected for collection, pytest should not abort the session because of that directory.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should remain resilient to unreadable directories that are outside the user's requested test scope. Running selected tests should continue normally instead of failing because pytest inspected an unrelated directory it cannot read.

constraints.grounded: The fix is limited to PermissionError encountered while determining whether a directory should be collected as a Python package. Directories that can be inspected and contain an initializer should still be collected as packages, and directories without that condition should remain uncollected as before.
constraints.conceptual: Only the unreadable-directory crash should be removed. Existing package discovery behavior for accessible directories should remain unchanged.

behavior: When pytest inspects a directory during collection and reading its package initializer status raises PermissionError, pytest skips collecting that directory instead of propagating the exception.
An unreadable directory that was not selected on the command line no longer prevents pytest from collecting and running the explicitly requested tests.
Accessible directories that qualify as Python packages continue to be collected as package nodes.
acceptance_criteria: When a project contains an unreadable sibling directory outside the selected test path, invoking pytest on the selected test path should not fail with PermissionError caused by that sibling directory.
When pytest encounters PermissionError while determining whether a directory is a package, it should treat that directory as not collectable and continue collection.
When a directory is accessible and contains a valid package initializer, pytest should still collect it as a package.

task_3.title: Preserve system-exit behavior during pytest collection
task_3.description: Pytest 8.2.1 changes collection-time exception handling so process-level exceptions are no longer absorbed as ordinary collection failures. Interrupting collection or exiting the process during collection now stops the run with the appropriate system-level behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest handles `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit` correctly when they occur during test collection, so the run stops immediately instead of treating them like normal collection errors.

expectation.grounded: During the collection phase, exceptions raised by a collector through `CallInfo.from_call(..., when="collect")` must preserve `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit` as re-raised system exceptions rather than converting them into ordinary `CollectReport` failures. Collection should terminate as soon as either exception occurs, with the corresponding interrupt or exit behavior remaining visible to users.
expectation.conceptual: If test discovery is interrupted by a user interrupt or an explicit process exit, pytest should stop discovery immediately and surface that interrupt or exit as such, rather than reporting it as a standard collection failure.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to collection-time handling of `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit`. Other collection outcomes and non-system exceptions should continue to follow existing passed, skipped, or failed collection reporting semantics.
constraints.conceptual: Only true system-level interruptions during discovery should get special handling. Normal collection results and ordinary collection errors should keep their existing behavior.

behavior: When a collector raises `KeyboardInterrupt` during collection, pytest stops the session instead of packaging the interruption as a normal collection error report.
When a collector raises `SystemExit` during collection, pytest stops the session instead of treating the exit as a standard collection failure.
Collection does not continue to later items after either of these system exceptions is raised during discovery.
Ordinary collection exceptions remain subject to the existing collection reporting flow.
acceptance_criteria: When a `KeyboardInterrupt` occurs while pytest is collecting tests, the run should terminate immediately and surface an interrupt outcome rather than a normal collection failure.
When a `SystemExit` occurs while pytest is collecting tests, the run should terminate immediately and surface an exit outcome rather than a normal collection failure.
When either of those exceptions is raised during collection, pytest should not continue collecting subsequent test modules or items.
When collection raises non-system exceptions, pytest should continue using its normal collection reporting behavior.

task_1.title: Add Python 3.13 compatibility and stricter pytester.makefile validation
task_1.description: The 8.2.1 update adds Python 3.13 support for runtime behaviors that depend on frame locals and makes invalid pytester file-creation calls fail explicitly when no extension is provided.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the library works correctly on Python 3.13 for traceback and pytester workflows that depend on frame-local state, and ensure that invalid `Pytester.makefile()` calls with `ext=None` are rejected explicitly.

expectation.grounded: On Python 3.13, behavior that reads frame locals in traceback processing and in `pytester` hook-recording checks must continue to work even when frame locals are exposed through a proxy-style mapping rather than a plain dict. `Pytester.makefile()` must raise `TypeError` when `ext` is `None` instead of accepting that input.
expectation.conceptual: The library should support Python 3.13 without breaking traceback analysis or `pytester` helper workflows because of changes in how Python exposes local variables. Invalid file-creation requests that omit an extension value entirely should fail clearly instead of being processed.

constraints.grounded: Existing behavior for supported Python versions must remain intact. Recursion detection in tracebacks must still treat repeated frames with equivalent local-variable state as recursive. Valid `Pytester.makefile()` calls with a real extension string must continue to follow the existing extension rules, with only `None` being newly rejected.
constraints.conceptual: The compatibility fix should preserve prior observable behavior outside the Python 3.13-specific locals change. Normal file creation through the helper should continue to work, and only clearly invalid missing-extension usage should be blocked.

behavior: On Python 3.13, traceback recursion detection continues to work when frame locals are no longer provided as a plain dict.
On Python 3.13, `pytester` hook-recording checks that evaluate against caller locals continue to work without failing because of the locals representation.
`Pytester.makefile()` now raises `TypeError` immediately when called with `ext=None`.
acceptance_criteria: When the library runs on Python 3.13 and traceback processing needs to compare local-variable state across repeated frames, it should still recognize recursion correctly.
When code uses `pytester` features that inspect recorded hook calls on Python 3.13, those checks should complete successfully without errors caused by non-dict frame locals.
When `Pytester.makefile()` is called with `ext=None`, it should raise `TypeError`.
When `Pytester.makefile()` is called with a valid extension string, it should continue to create files under the existing extension-validation rules.

task_4.title: Handle read-only squashfuse_ll mounts without crashing
task_4.description: The update makes cache directory setup tolerate a read-only filesystem condition reported as 'Function not implemented' under squashfuse_ll, so the library no longer crashes in that environment and instead degrades gracefully.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running the library on a read-only squashfuse_ll mount does not crash when cache directories cannot be created, and that this condition is treated the same way as other read-only filesystem failures.

expectation.grounded: During assertion rewrite cache directory creation, pytest should treat an OSError with errno.ENOSYS from a squashfuse_ll read-only mount as a recoverable read-only filesystem condition, the same as errno.EROFS. In this path, directory creation should be reported as unsuccessful rather than raising, while unrelated OSError values should still propagate.
expectation.conceptual: When the runtime is on a read-only filesystem that reports the failure using 'Function not implemented' instead of a standard read-only error, the library should skip cache directory creation and continue operating instead of crashing.

constraints.grounded: Only read-only-equivalent cache-directory creation failures should be suppressed in this flow. errno.EROFS and errno.ENOSYS are non-fatal here; other OSError errno values must preserve existing exception behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Treat only recognized read-only mount failures as recoverable, and do not hide unrelated filesystem errors.

behavior: Assertion rewrite cache directory creation interprets OSError with errno.ENOSYS as a read-only filesystem failure when encountered under squashfuse_ll.
In that ENOSYS case, the cache directory creation step fails gracefully instead of aborting execution with an exception.
Existing handling for standard read-only filesystem errors remains intact.
Filesystem errors other than the recognized read-only cases continue to raise normally.
acceptance_criteria: When the library runs from a read-only squashfuse_ll mount and cache directory creation raises OSError with errno.ENOSYS, it should continue running without crashing.
When cache directory creation raises OSError with errno.EROFS, it should continue to be treated as a recoverable read-only condition.
When cache directory creation raises an unrelated OSError errno, the error should still be surfaced rather than being silently ignored.

task_5.title: Restore default .pytest_cache directory permissions
task_5.description: Pytest 8.2.1 fixes a regression from 8.2.0 where automatically created .pytest_cache directories were created with overly restrictive owner-only permissions. Cache directories now use normal directory permissions derived from the active umask so CI systems and other tools can traverse them as expected.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that automatically created .pytest_cache directories no longer use owner-only permissions after upgrading to pytest 8.2.1, and instead remain accessible according to normal system defaults so repository-scanning tools do not fail with permission errors.

expectation.grounded: When pytest's cache subsystem creates the .pytest_cache directory, including creation triggered by cache usage such as config.cache.mkdir(), the directory should receive the default directory access bits implied by the current process umask rather than an owner-only mode. In typical environments using umask 022, the resulting .pytest_cache permissions should match a standard rwxr-xr-x directory, avoiding permission-denied failures from external filesystem scans.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest-created cache directories should behave like ordinary project directories: accessible to other tools according to the environment's normal permission policy, instead of becoming unexpectedly private to the current user.

constraints.grounded: The fix should affect automatically created cache directories without changing the public cache API shape. Permission handling must respect the active umask, including more restrictive settings, rather than forcing a single fixed mode in every environment.
constraints.conceptual: The change should remove the regression without making cache directory permissions broader than the system would normally allow, and without changing how users interact with pytest's cache feature.

behavior: On creation, the top-level .pytest_cache directory uses normal directory permissions derived from the current umask instead of owner-only permissions.
Cache directory creation through pytest's cache API yields a .pytest_cache parent directory whose access bits align with other newly created directories in the same environment.
Tools that recursively inspect the repository can traverse .pytest_cache when the environment's permission policy allows it, instead of failing because pytest created the directory too restrictively.
acceptance_criteria: Given an environment with a typical umask of 022, when pytest creates .pytest_cache, then the directory should be group-readable and world-readable/traversable rather than limited to the owner.
Given an environment with a more restrictive umask, when pytest creates .pytest_cache, then the resulting directory permissions should still follow that umask.

When a CI system or other filesystem-scanning tool examines a repository after pytest has created .pytest_cache, it should not encounter a permission-denied error caused by pytest assigning owner-only permissions to that directory.

task_6.title: Add provenance attestation for published pytest artifacts
task_6.description: Pytest 8.2.1 adds verifiable provenance metadata for its published source and wheel distributions so users can confirm the official packages came from the project’s release pipeline. The update affects package distribution trust and supply-chain verification, not pytest runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users upgrading to pytest 8.2.1 can verify the provenance of official pytest distribution artifacts, including both source distributions and wheels, without changing pytest’s runtime behavior.

expectation.grounded: Pytest 8.2.1 release artifacts should include verifiable package provenance attestation for the published sdist and wheel distributions, allowing consumers to validate artifact origin using GitHub Artifact Attestation support. No public pytest runtime API, test execution semantics, or error behavior changes are evidenced in the provided patch inputs.
expectation.conceptual: Official pytest packages for this release should be accompanied by verifiable provenance metadata so users and automation can confirm the packages were produced by the trusted release process. Upgrading should not otherwise change how pytest behaves at runtime.

constraints.grounded: The change scope is limited to release artifact provenance for published distributions. It must not introduce observable changes to pytest command behavior, collection, execution, warnings, exceptions, or public APIs based on the provided release materials.
constraints.conceptual: This update should improve package trust and verification only. Existing pytest usage and behavior should remain unchanged for end users.

behavior: Published pytest 8.2.1 source and wheel artifacts are expected to carry provenance attestation that can be verified by consumers.
The update adds a supply-chain verification capability for official distribution artifacts rather than a new pytest runtime feature.
No user-visible runtime behavior change is indicated for pytest execution, configuration, or APIs in the provided materials.
acceptance_criteria: When a user obtains an official pytest 8.2.1 sdist or wheel, it should be possible to verify that artifact’s provenance through the release attestation mechanism referenced by the project.
When users upgrade from pytest 8.2.0 to 8.2.1, pytest command-line behavior and runtime semantics should remain unchanged.
The upgrade should provide additional trust metadata for official packages without requiring users to change existing pytest usage patterns.
